posts.title: What Is Nostr?
posts.description: A plain-language introduction to Nostr — the open protocol that lets you own your identity and communicate without relying on any single company or server.
posts.excerpt: Nostr is a simple, open protocol for decentralized communication. No company owns it. No server controls it. Here's how it works.
posts.seoTitle: What Is Nostr? A Beginner's Guide to the Open Protocol
posts.seoDescription: Learn what Nostr is, how it works, and why it matters. A plain-language introduction for professionals who want to understand decentralized communication.
posts.content:
Nostr stands for **Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays**. It is an open protocol — a set of rules — that lets people publish messages, build profiles, and communicate without depending on any single company.

No corporation runs Nostr. No one can shut it down. And no one can take away your account.

![When you post on Nostr, your note is broadcast to multiple independent relay servers simultaneously — no single server owns your content](/images/guides/what-is-nostr/broadcast-diagram.svg)

## How It Works

Every social platform you've used — LinkedIn, X, Instagram — works the same way: you create an account on their servers, and they control everything. Your posts, your followers, your data, your access. If the company goes down, changes its rules, or decides to ban you, there's nothing you can do.

Nostr works differently. It has two core concepts: **keys** and **relays**.

### Keys: Your Identity

When you join Nostr, you get a pair of cryptographic keys — think of them as a lock and a key.

- Your **public key** is your identity. It's like a username that belongs to you permanently. Anyone can see it.
- Your **private key** is your password. It proves you are who you say you are. Only you should ever have it.

These keys are not stored on anyone's server. They are generated on your device. No company issues them, and no company can revoke them. Your identity is yours.

<Callout type="tip">
Your public key starts with `npub` and your private key starts with `nsec`. Treat your private key like a bank password — never share it, never paste it into a website.
</Callout>

### Relays: The Network

Relays are simple servers that pass messages around. When you publish a post, your app sends it to one or more relays. When someone wants to read your posts, their app fetches them from those relays.

Here's the critical difference: **you are not locked into any single relay.** You can use one, five, or fifty. If a relay goes offline, your other relays still have your data. If a relay starts censoring content, you switch to a different one. No relay is "the Nostr server" — they are all interchangeable.

Think of it like email. Your email isn't trapped inside Gmail. You can use any provider, and they all talk to each other. Nostr works on a similar principle, but simpler and without needing to register anywhere.

![You choose which relays to use and can switch anytime — if one goes down, the others still have your posts](/images/guides/what-is-nostr/relay-nodes.svg)

## Why It Matters

The traditional internet is built on concentration. A handful of cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Cloudflare) host most of the services you use every day. When one of them fails, huge swaths of the internet go dark — as the world saw repeatedly in late 2025.

Nostr eliminates that single point of failure. There is no central server to go down, no corporate policy to change overnight, and no account to get suspended.

For professionals, this means:

- **Your content is portable.** Switch apps anytime — your posts and followers come with you.
- **Your identity is permanent.** No platform can delete your profile or lock you out.
- **Your network is resilient.** It works even when major infrastructure fails.

Nostr is not a company or a product. It is a protocol — like email or the web itself. Anyone can build on it. And that's exactly what makes it durable.

posts.title: Why Nostr Is Resilient (And the Internet Isn't)
posts.description: The 2025 cloud outages took down X, ChatGPT, LinkedIn, and public transit. Nostr's architecture is built to survive exactly this kind of failure.
posts.excerpt: AWS, Azure, and Cloudflare all failed in late 2025 — and took half the internet with them. Here's why Nostr doesn't have that problem.
posts.seoTitle: Why Nostr Is Resilient — And the Internet Isn't
posts.seoDescription: The 2025 cloud outages revealed how fragile the internet really is. Learn how Nostr's relay architecture avoids single points of failure by design.
posts.content:
In late 2025, three of the biggest cloud infrastructure providers — AWS, Azure, and Cloudflare — all experienced major outages. Not at the same time. But close enough to make a point.

When AWS went down, it didn't just affect Amazon. It took out streaming services, banking apps, and enterprise tools that millions of people rely on daily. When Azure failed, Microsoft's own products went dark — and so did the businesses built on top of them. When Cloudflare had issues, websites and APIs around the world became unreachable.

X went offline. ChatGPT went offline. LinkedIn went offline. Public transit systems in some cities stopped displaying real-time information. Not because of a cyberattack. Because a single provider had a bad day.

![When a major cloud provider fails, every service built on top of it goes down simultaneously — social media, AI tools, enterprise software, banking APIs](/images/guides/why-nostr-is-resilient/outage-timeline.svg)

## The Problem: Single Points of Failure

The modern internet looks decentralized on the surface. Millions of websites, apps, and services. But underneath, most of them run on a surprisingly small number of providers.

Think of it like a city's power grid. Hundreds of buildings, each with their own lights and systems. But if they all draw from the same power plant, one failure blacks out the entire city.

That's what happened in 2025. The "buildings" were different — X, LinkedIn, ChatGPT, transit apps — but they were all drawing from the same infrastructure. When that infrastructure failed, everything went dark together.

This isn't a bug. It's the architecture. Centralized platforms depend on centralized infrastructure. They have no choice.

## How Nostr Avoids This

Nostr works differently. It runs on many independent **relays** — simple servers operated by different people, in different locations, on different infrastructure.

When you publish a post on Nostr, your app sends it to multiple relays. Those relays are not owned by the same company. They don't run on the same cloud provider. They don't share a single point of failure.

If one relay goes down, the others keep working. Your posts are still accessible. Your identity still exists. The network keeps running — because it was never dependent on any single node.

<Callout type="tip">
You choose which relays to use. Most Nostr apps connect to several by default, giving you built-in redundancy without any extra setup.
</Callout>

![Centralized vs Nostr: when a single server fails everything collapses — on Nostr one relay goes down while the others keep your posts alive](/images/guides/why-nostr-is-resilient/centralized-vs-nostr.svg)

## No Company, No Kill Switch

There's a deeper point here. Every platform you use today exists at the discretion of the company that runs it.

Twitter became X because one person decided it should. LinkedIn can change its algorithm, its rules, or its terms of service overnight. If a platform decides your account violates policy — or if they simply make an error — you lose access to your network, your content, and your professional presence. There is no appeal that's guaranteed to work.

Nostr has none of these risks because there is no company behind it. Nostr is a protocol — an open standard, like email or HTTP. No one owns it. No one can change the rules for everyone. No one can flip a switch and turn it off.

Your identity on Nostr is a cryptographic key pair that you control. Not a username registered on someone else's database. It can't be suspended, revoked, or deleted by a third party.

## What This Means for You

If the platforms you depend on for professional communication went offline tomorrow — no LinkedIn, no email, no Slack — could you still reach your network?

For most people, the answer is no. And that's a risk worth thinking about.

Nostr doesn't require you to abandon the tools you use today. But it offers something none of them can: **a communication layer that no single failure can take down.** Your posts exist across multiple relays. Your identity lives on your device. Your network is resilient by design, not by promise.

The 2025 outages weren't a one-time event. They were a preview. The question is whether you're building on infrastructure that can handle the next one.

posts.title: Nostr for Beginners: Your First Steps
posts.description: A practical, step-by-step guide to getting started on Nostr. Create your identity with the Nostr WoT Extension, pick a client to explore the network, and start following people — all in about ten minutes.
posts.excerpt: Ready to try Nostr? Start by creating your identity with the Nostr WoT Extension, then pick a client to explore the network and find people to follow.
posts.seoTitle: Nostr for Beginners: Your First Steps
posts.seoDescription: A beginner's guide to Nostr. Create your identity with the WoT Extension, choose a client, connect to relays, and start following people in minutes.
posts.content:
This guide will get you up and running on Nostr in about ten minutes. No technical background required. By the end, you'll have your own identity, a client to explore the network, and people to follow.

## Step 1: Understand What You're Creating

On Nostr, your identity is a **key pair** — a public key and a private key. Think of it this way:

- **Public key (npub):** Your address. Share it freely. People use it to find and follow you.
- **Private key (nsec):** Your master password. It proves you own your identity. Never share it with anyone.

There is no email registration. No phone number. No company holding your account. You generate these keys, and they are yours permanently.

## Step 2: Create Your Identity with the Nostr WoT Extension

The best way to start on Nostr is by creating your identity with the **Nostr WoT Extension**. It acts as your key manager and signer — it keeps your private key safe in the browser and lets any Nostr client use it without ever exposing it.

<Callout type="tip">
Think of the extension as your Nostr wallet. Clients are just windows into the network — your identity lives in the extension, not in any single app.
</Callout>

1. Install the extension from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/nostr-wot-extension/nfhdbhnnbibgkfipjbmdgcbhhjdpajjl) or [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/nostr-wot/).
2. Click the extension icon and follow the setup wizard.
3. Choose **Create New Keys** — the extension generates a 24-word seed phrase for you.
4. Write down your 24 words and store them somewhere safe. This is your master backup.
5. Set a local password to encrypt your keys in the browser.
6. Fill in your profile: display name, bio, and avatar.

<Callout type="warning">
Your 24-word seed phrase is the only way to recover your account. If you lose it, there is no "forgot password" option. Store it offline — a piece of paper in a safe place or a password manager works fine.
</Callout>

For a detailed walkthrough of the extension setup, see the [Getting Started guide](/guides/getting-started).

## Step 3: Pick a Client to Explore the Network

With your identity created in the extension, you're ready to explore Nostr. A "client" is an app that lets you read posts, follow people, and publish content. Your identity works across all of them — switching clients never means losing your account.

Here are solid options:

**On desktop (web browser):**
- [Coracle](https://coracle.social) — Lightweight, focused on simplicity. Great starting point.
- [Primal](https://primal.net) — Polished interface, works in any browser.

**On mobile:**
- [Damus](https://damus.io) — iOS only. One of the most popular Nostr apps.
- [Amethyst](https://github.com/vitorpamplona/amethyst) — Android only. Full-featured.
- [Primal](https://primal.net/downloads) — Available for iOS and Android.

When you open any of these clients, they will ask for your Nostr identity. Choose "Login with extension" (NIP-07) — the client will connect to the Nostr WoT Extension automatically.

![Primal, Coracle, Damus, and Amethyst — four solid Nostr clients to start with across web, iOS, and Android](/images/guides/nostr-for-beginners/client-comparison.svg)

## Step 4: Connect to Relays

Relays are the servers that store and deliver your posts. Most clients come pre-configured with a default set, so you probably don't need to change anything right away.

If you want to check or adjust your relays:

1. Open your client's settings.
2. Look for a "Relays" section.
3. Make sure you're connected to at least 3–5 relays for good coverage.

Popular relays include `wss://relay.damus.io`, `wss://relay.primal.net`, and `wss://nos.lol`.

<Callout type="tip">
You don't need to understand relays in depth to get started. Just make sure your client is connected to a few. You can fine-tune this later as you learn more.
</Callout>

![Your client connects to multiple independent relay servers — your posts are stored across all of them simultaneously](/images/guides/nostr-for-beginners/relays-diagram.svg)

## Step 5: Follow People

Nostr is better with a feed. Here's how to find people:

- **Search by name** in your client's search bar.
- **Paste an npub** (public key) directly to find a specific person.
- **Browse trending posts** — most clients have a discover or trending section.
- **Check who others follow** — find one person you know and look at their follow list.

## Step 6: Post Something

You're set up. Say hello. The Nostr community actively welcomes newcomers.

Your post goes out to your connected relays. Anyone following you — or browsing those relays — can see it. No algorithm decides who sees your content.

## What's Next

You now have a working Nostr identity and a feed to browse. A few things worth exploring next:

- **Web of Trust:** As you follow people and they follow you back, you're building a trust network. The extension helps you visualize and manage it — useful once you have some connections. Learn more in [Understanding WoT](/guides/understanding-wot).
- **Zaps:** Nostr supports instant Bitcoin micropayments called "zaps." You can tip posts you like. This requires a Lightning wallet — see the [Setting Up a Wallet](/guides/setting-up-wallet) guide.
- **Multiple clients:** Try different apps. Your identity works across all of them. Find the one that fits how you use social media.

The most important thing: Nostr is a protocol, not a platform. There's no algorithm to game, no company to please, and no single point of failure. Your presence here is yours to build — and yours to keep.

posts.title: Getting started: choose your Nostr account setup
posts.description: Install Nostr WoT and choose a new identity, an existing key or backup, a watch-only account, or a QR connection to an external signer.
posts.excerpt: Install Nostr WoT and choose a new identity, an existing key or backup, a watch-only account, or a QR connection to an external signer.
posts.seoTitle: Getting started: choose your Nostr account setup
posts.seoDescription: Install Nostr WoT and choose a new identity, an existing key or backup, a watch-only account, or a QR connection to an external signer.
posts.content:
Nostr WoT offers four ways to set up an identity. If this is your first Nostr account, start with **Create New**. If you already have an identity, choose the method that matches what you have.

## Install and open the extension

1. Open the [download page](/download) and follow the store link for your browser.
2. Install the extension and pin it to your browser toolbar so you can find it again.
3. Open the Nostr WoT popup and select **Continue** to reach the account methods.

## Choose your method

| What you have | Method | Follow this guide |
|---|---|---|
| No Nostr identity yet | **Create New** | [Create an account and save your 24 recovery words](/guides/create-nostr-account) |
| A private key, recovery phrase, or encrypted backup | **Import Key or Backup** | [Restore an existing identity](/guides/import-nostr-account) |
| Only a public key, and you want to explore | **Watch-Only** | [Add a read-only account](/guides/watch-only-nostr-account) |
| An identity in an external NIP-46 signer | **Nostr Connect** | [Connect your signer with a QR code](/guides/connect-nostr-signer) |

Creating a new identity does not require an email address or phone number. Your keys identify you on Nostr. Importing restores the identity represented by your existing key; creating a new one gives you a different identity.

## Understand what to keep

**Public key (npub):** identifies your account and can be shared. **Private key (nsec) or recovery phrase:** lets someone control the identity and must remain private. **Local vault password:** protects access to keys stored in this browser; it cannot replace a lost recovery phrase.

<Callout type="warning">
Never use recovery words shown in a tutorial or demonstration. For a new account, save the words generated by your own extension before continuing.
</Callout>

## After setup

Open the popup and check that the public key matches the identity you intended to use. With a signing account, visit a Nostr client and review the extension's permission prompts when connecting. Watch-only accounts cannot sign posts.

Continue with [identity management](/guides/managing-identity), [site permissions](/guides/site-permissions), or [the Web of Trust](/guides/understanding-wot). You can set up a [Lightning wallet](/guides/setting-up-wallet) separately when you are ready to use zaps.

## Account previews and finishing setup

The completion screen puts the account summary and **Get Started** at the bottom. It shows the account name and a copyable public key; only derived sub-accounts are described as sharing the main seed phrase. New accounts can use global rules or copy site overrides from another account. Authentication grants stay separate.

posts.title: Create a Nostr account with 24 recovery words
posts.description: Create a new Nostr identity in the extension popup, verify your recovery backup and protect this browser with a local vault password.
posts.excerpt: Create a new Nostr identity in the extension popup, verify your recovery backup and protect this browser with a local vault password.
posts.seoTitle: Create a Nostr account with 24 recovery words
posts.seoDescription: Create a new Nostr identity in the extension popup, verify your recovery backup and protect this browser with a local vault password.
posts.content:
Choose **Create New** when you want a new Nostr identity. The extension generates 24 recovery words and derives your keys from them. You do not need to enter an email address or phone number.

## Create and back up your identity

1. Open the extension popup. On first setup, select **Continue**, then **Create New**.
2. Reveal your recovery phrase in a private place. Write all **24 words in their exact order** and store them securely.
3. Use the backup controls if you want a file copy. A plain-text download contains the unencrypted phrase; protect it accordingly. An encrypted backup needs its own backup password.
4. Confirm that you have saved the phrase. Complete the backup check by filling the missing words from your own saved copy.

<Callout type="warning">
Anyone with your recovery words can recover this identity. Keep them private. Do not use words from a video, screenshot or another person's account. There is no email reset that can replace a lost phrase.
</Callout>

## Protect this browser

5. Choose a timed auto-lock setting, then set and confirm a local vault password. Keep the password somewhere you can recover it.
6. Continue through the remaining setup. Follow suggestions are optional; skip them if you prefer to choose people later.
7. At the completion screen, select **Get Started**. Check your public key in the popup, then lock the vault when you finish.

The vault password unlocks this browser's stored keys. Your recovery phrase restores the identity. Save both, and do not treat one as a substitute for the other.

Already have the identity you want? Use [Import Key or Backup](/guides/import-nostr-account) instead of creating another one. [Compare all four setup methods](/guides/getting-started).

## Account previews and finishing setup

When a main recovery phrase already exists, **Create New** opens **New Sub-Account**. It uses that phrase with another derivation path; it does not generate a second recovery phrase. Edit the name if needed. The npub and hex public keys appear below their labels in accent color, shortened in the middle. Copy icons copy the complete values. **Advanced** sits below the keys and opens the path editor; leave the proposed path unless you need a specific one.

Follow suggestions show names and small pictures from verified public profiles when available. The extension reuses a shared cache for 30 minutes, keeping at most 500 profiles, and looks up missing metadata at purplepag.es. The public author key is sent to that directory; images load separately from the profile's image host. Missing profiles fall back to a shortened key. Loading does not block selection or **Skip for now**.

The completion screen puts the account summary and **Get Started** at the bottom. It shows the account name and a copyable public key; only derived sub-accounts are described as sharing the main seed phrase. New accounts can use global rules or copy site overrides from another account. Authentication grants stay separate.

posts.title: Import a Nostr private key or recovery backup
posts.description: Restore an existing Nostr identity from an nsec, hex private key, recovery phrase, ncryptsec or supported encrypted backup.
posts.excerpt: Restore an existing Nostr identity from an nsec, hex private key, recovery phrase, ncryptsec or supported encrypted backup.
posts.seoTitle: Import a Nostr private key or recovery backup
posts.seoDescription: Restore an existing Nostr identity from an nsec, hex private key, recovery phrase, ncryptsec or supported encrypted backup.
posts.content:
Choose **Import Key or Backup** to bring an existing identity into this browser. You need its private key, recovery phrase or a supported encrypted backup. An npub is a public key and belongs in [Watch-Only](/guides/watch-only-nostr-account).

## Restore your existing identity

1. Open the extension popup and choose **Import Key or Backup** from the setup methods.
2. Paste your **nsec**, hex private key, or recovery phrase into the import field, or load your supported backup file. The extension detects the format.
3. For an **ncryptsec** or encrypted backup, enter the password used to encrypt it. This is the backup's password, not necessarily your browser vault password.
4. Continue after the format is recognized. If the extension reports an error, check the input and password before trying again. Keep the original backup intact.
5. Keep your existing recovery backup safe. Set the local vault password when prompted. If this browser already has a vault, unlock it with its existing password when asked.
6. Finish setup and compare the displayed public key with the npub of the identity you intended to restore.

## Recovery phrases and encrypted files

Existing 12-word and 24-word recovery phrases can be imported. A new identity generated by the extension uses 24 words. If your identity used a custom derivation path, keep that path and expected public key with your recovery records; see [custom identity paths](/guides/custom-identity-paths).

Importing a phrase starts with its first Nostr key; it does not automatically restore every sub-account or custom path. Read the import screen's seed notice: when the unlocked vault already has a main recovery phrase, only the first key from the additional phrase is imported, rather than storing it as another main seed.

An encrypted file's password protects that file. Setting a new local vault password does not change the password of an existing backup.

<Callout type="warning">
Enter private keys and recovery words only in the extension's import interface. Never send them to someone offering to help restore an account.
</Callout>

Prefer to keep signing in another app? Use [Nostr Connect](/guides/connect-nostr-signer). [Compare all four setup methods](/guides/getting-started).

posts.title: Add a watch-only Nostr account
posts.description: Use an npub to explore a Nostr identity without importing its private key. Understand what a watch-only account can and cannot do.
posts.excerpt: Use an npub to explore a Nostr identity without importing its private key. Understand what a watch-only account can and cannot do.
posts.seoTitle: Add a watch-only Nostr account
posts.seoDescription: Use an npub to explore a Nostr identity without importing its private key. Understand what a watch-only account can and cannot do.
posts.content:
Choose **Watch-Only** when you have a public key and want to view an identity without importing its private key. This is useful for exploring a profile and its trust network before connecting a signing account.

## Add the public key

1. Copy the **npub** of the identity you want to view. Check that it belongs to the intended profile.
2. Open the extension popup and select **Watch-Only** from the setup methods.
3. Paste the public key into the field and select **Continue**. If validation fails, check that you copied the complete public key.
4. Finish setup and confirm that the displayed identity matches the npub you entered. Allow time for profile information to load from relays.

## Know the limits

A public key can identify an account but cannot authorize an action as that account. Watch-only mode cannot sign events, publish posts, or approve signing requests for that identity. Adding someone else's public key does not give you control of their account.

You do not need that person's private key to view their public identity. Never ask someone to send you an nsec or recovery phrase for this purpose.

## When you want to sign

If the identity is yours, use [Import Key or Backup](/guides/import-nostr-account) with its private material, or [Nostr Connect](/guides/connect-nostr-signer) with a signer that controls it. Confirm the public key after connecting so you do not confuse two different identities.

If you do not yet have your own identity, [create a new account](/guides/create-nostr-account). [Compare all four setup methods](/guides/getting-started).

posts.title: Connect a Nostr signer with a QR code
posts.description: Use Nostr Connect to pair the extension with an external NIP-46 signer. Scan the QR code, approve the connection and keep signing in your signer.
posts.excerpt: Use Nostr Connect to pair the extension with an external NIP-46 signer. Scan the QR code, approve the connection and keep signing in your signer.
posts.seoTitle: Connect a Nostr signer with a QR code
posts.seoDescription: Use Nostr Connect to pair the extension with an external NIP-46 signer. Scan the QR code, approve the connection and keep signing in your signer.
posts.content:
Choose **Nostr Connect** when your Nostr identity is controlled by an external NIP-46 signer. The extension connects to that signer; your identity's signing key stays with it.

## Before you begin

Have your signer available and unlocked, with the identity you intend to use. It must support the NIP-46 connection method offered here. You do not need to paste your private key into the extension for this flow.

## Connect by scanning the QR code

1. Open the extension popup and select **Nostr Connect** from the setup methods.
2. Keep the **QR Code** tab selected. Wait for the code to appear and the **Waiting for connection...** status.
3. In your signer, open its connection or QR-scanning function and scan the code displayed by this extension. Use the signer's instructions if its controls have different names.
4. Review the connection request in your signer, confirm the intended identity and approve it there.
5. Wait for the extension to recognize the connection and advance. Set or unlock the local vault when prompted, then finish setup and check that the displayed public key matches your signer identity.

## If scanning is not available

**Copy URI** provides the same connection request for a signer that supports opening a Nostr Connect URI. If your signer supplies a `bunker://` connection address instead, use the separate **Bunker URL** tab. Choose the tab that matches the connection method supported by your signer.

## If the connection expires

Keep the signer available and check its pending requests. If the extension displays a timeout or failure, select **Try again** and scan the fresh code. An old screenshot is not a reusable recovery backup.

Keep your signer and its own recovery backup accessible. An extension vault password cannot recover a private key held by an external signer.

[Compare all four setup methods](/guides/getting-started), or learn how to [review site permissions](/guides/site-permissions).

QR Code and Bunker URL are separate tabs, with space before their content. Switch to Bunker URL to paste the connection supplied by your signer. Never paste an nsec or recovery phrase into that field.

posts.title: Managing Your Identity
posts.description: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension manages your Nostr identity with NIP-07 signer support, profile management, and essential key security practices.
posts.excerpt: Your Nostr identity is the foundation of everything in the extension. Learn to manage your keys, profile, and signer settings.
posts.seoTitle: Managing Your Identity — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension manages your Nostr identity with NIP-07 signer support, profile management, and essential key security practices.
posts.content:
Your Nostr identity is the anchor for everything else in the extension — your trust network, your wallet, your permissions. This guide covers how to manage that identity, keep your keys secure, and use the NIP-07 signer that lets websites interact with your Nostr account.

## NIP-07 Signer Support


NIP-07 is the standard that allows Nostr web applications to request signatures from a browser extension without ever seeing your private key. When you visit a Nostr client like Primal, Snort, or Coracle, it can ask the extension to sign events on your behalf.

Here is how it works in practice:

1. A website calls `window.nostr.getPublicKey()` to identify you.
2. When you post a note or update your profile, the site sends the unsigned event to the extension.
3. You see a permission prompt. If you approve, the extension signs it with your private key and sends back the signature.
4. Your private key never leaves the extension.

<Callout type="tip">
If you previously used another NIP-07 extension like nos2x or Alby, disable it before using Nostr WoT. Only one NIP-07 signer should be active at a time to avoid conflicts.
</Callout>

## Managing Your Nostr Profile

Open the extension and choose **Edit profile** in the Account section. Edit your display name, biography, picture, cover image and optional public fields. The picture and cover controls open the image editor; their high-contrast labels remain visible over both light and dark photos.

Review the preview before confirming publication. The extension signs and publishes a kind:0 profile event with the active identity and updates its local profile cache. Other clients must fetch the new event before displaying the changes; propagation time depends on their relays and caches. Profile fields are public. Keep recovery words and private keys out of them.

## Key Security Best Practices

Your seed phrase and nsec (private key) are the single most important pieces of data in your Nostr identity. Anyone who has either one controls your account — they can post as you, change your profile, and access your contacts. There is no password reset, no support team to call.

### Storage

- The extension encrypts your keys locally using your encryption password. They are never stored in plain text.
- Back up your 24-word seed phrase in a password manager or write it on paper and store it somewhere safe.
- Never share your seed phrase or nsec with anyone, paste them into a website, or send them in a DM.

### Encryption Password

- Choose a strong, unique password when setting up the extension.
- The extension locks after a period of inactivity. You will need this password to unlock it.
- If you forget this password, you can restore access using your 24-word seed phrase.


### Multiple Devices

If you use the extension on multiple browsers or machines, restore from your 24-word seed phrase on each one. Your identity is tied to your key pair, not to any single device.

<Callout type="tip">
Your seed phrase works independently of any single browser or device. Keep it in a safe place and you can always restore your full Nostr identity.
</Callout>

## Switching Between Identities

The extension supports multiple identities. If you manage more than one Nostr account, switch between them from the Identity tab by clicking your profile avatar. Each identity has its own trust graph, wallet, and permission settings.

## What's Next?

With your identity secured, it is time to understand how the extension uses it to build your [Web of Trust](/guides/understanding-wot). If you want to connect a wallet, jump to [Setting Up Your Wallet](/guides/setting-up-wallet).

## Account previews and finishing setup

When a main recovery phrase already exists, **Create New** opens **New Sub-Account**. It uses that phrase with another derivation path; it does not generate a second recovery phrase. Edit the name if needed. The npub and hex public keys appear below their labels in accent color, shortened in the middle. Copy icons copy the complete values. **Advanced** sits below the keys and opens the path editor; leave the proposed path unless you need a specific one.

Follow suggestions show names and small pictures from verified public profiles when available. The extension reuses a shared cache for 30 minutes, keeping at most 500 profiles, and looks up missing metadata at purplepag.es. The public author key is sent to that directory; images load separately from the profile's image host. Missing profiles fall back to a shortened key. Loading does not block selection or **Skip for now**.

The completion screen puts the account summary and **Get Started** at the bottom. It shows the account name and a copyable public key; only derived sub-accounts are described as sharing the main seed phrase. New accounts can use global rules or copy site overrides from another account. Authentication grants stay separate.

posts.title: Removing an Account
posts.description: Remove a Nostr account safely: back up its key or seed and derivation path, review the confirmation, and understand what remains on relays and other devices.
posts.excerpt: Remove a Nostr account safely: back up its key or seed and derivation path, review the confirmation, and understand what remains on relays and other devices.
posts.seoTitle: Removing an Account — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Remove a Nostr account safely: back up its key or seed and derivation path, review the confirmation, and understand what remains on relays and other devices.
posts.content:
Removing an account deletes its local entry from this extension. It does not delete its profile or posts from Nostr relays, or remove the identity from your other devices.

## Back up before removing

Open **Settings → Security**. Keep a secure copy of the private key or encrypted backup. For a derived account, keep the recovery phrase **and its derivation path**. An imported key also needs a backup; importing it does not prove that you still have another copy.

![Security settings with recovery phrase and encrypted-backup options](/images/guides/extension/security.png)

## Remove the account

1. Open the account selector at the top of the popup.
2. Find the account and select its **×** remove icon on the right.
3. Read the confirmation and check the account name. For seed-derived accounts, the dialog also shows the derivation path and explains how other accounts using that phrase are affected.
4. Select **Remove** to confirm, or **Cancel** to keep the account. There is no requirement to type REMOVE.

![Account selector with a remove icon beside each account](/images/guides/extension/accounts.png)

![Removal confirmation for a derived demo account, including its derivation path](/images/guides/extension/remove-confirmation.png)

Removing one derived account leaves the other accounts from the same seed available. To stop using that seed in this extension, remove every account derived from it. Keep your backup before doing so.

## Restore an identity

Open the account selector, choose **Add Account → Import Key or Backup**, and use your saved key or recovery phrase. To recover a specific derived identity, use its original derivation path. Do not assume that restoring keys also restores local permissions or wallet connections.

See [Import a Nostr account](/guides/import-nostr-account) and [Custom identity paths](/guides/custom-identity-paths).

posts.title: Name your Nostr identities and choose a custom path
posts.description: Use optional identity names, advanced derivation paths and public-key previews in Nostr WoT. Learn what to keep for recovery.
posts.excerpt: Use optional identity names, advanced derivation paths and public-key previews in Nostr WoT. Learn what to keep for recovery.
posts.seoTitle: Name your Nostr identities and choose a custom path
posts.seoDescription: Use optional identity names, advanced derivation paths and public-key previews in Nostr WoT. Learn what to keep for recovery.
posts.content:
A work identity, a project identity and a testing identity do not have to look identical in your account list. Nostr WoT lets you give a new seed-derived identity a useful local name and, under **Advanced**, choose the derivation path yourself. Leave the path alone if the automatic choice suits you.

## A name and a path do different jobs

| Setting | What it changes |
|---|---|
| Account name | A local label that helps you recognize the identity. It is optional and does not change the key or publish a profile name. |
| Derivation path | The route used to derive a key from your existing seed. A different path normally produces a different identity. |
| npub and hex preview | Two representations of the resulting public key, shown before you save. |

## Create the identity

1. Unlock the extension and open the account selector. Start adding an account and choose **HD Sub-Account**. This requires an existing recovery phrase in the vault; an imported nsec alone is not that phrase.
2. The extension proposes the next unused path from your main recovery phrase. The relationship is explained below the form; there is no separate source-seed row.
3. Optionally enter a name such as “Project” or “Testing”. Leaving it blank keeps the proposed name.
4. Open **Advanced** only if you need a specific path. Enter the exact path and wait for the public-key preview to refresh.
5. Check both the path and the displayed npub. An invalid path, failed preview or preview still loading prevents continuation.
6. Select **Continue** to save the identity in the vault. Editing the preview alone does not save an account.

## What does a path look like?

The initial Nostr path is `m/44'/1237'/0'/0/0`. An example later path in the extension’s sequence is `m/44'/1237'/0'/0/1`. These are paths, not private keys. Keep every slash, number and apostrophe when recording yours.

For recovery in another tool, never assume its account counter follows the same sequence. [NIP-06](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/06.md) describes incrementing the hardened account component; the extension’s existing additional-account sequence increments the final component. Matching the exact path and public key matters more than matching an account number. NIP-06 is currently marked optional and unrecommended by its maintainers, so support across clients is not guaranteed.

Recognized network-prefix hints describe a convention only. Choosing a Bitcoin-looking path still creates a Nostr identity, not a Bitcoin wallet. Avoid reusing a path already used by a wallet.

## Keep recovery practical

Store your recovery phrase securely, together with the exact path and the public npub you expect to recover. A local name is useful for organization but cannot restore a key. A seed alone does not tell another application which custom path you selected.

Different paths are useful for organizing identities, not for isolating them from compromise of their shared seed. They do not guarantee anonymity either. Changing the path does not transfer posts, followers or profile information to the new identity. Existing keys are not changed by this feature.

Start with [identity management](/guides/managing-identity) if you only need account switching. Use custom paths when you have a recovery or organization requirement you can document.

## Account previews and finishing setup

When a main recovery phrase already exists, **Create New** opens **New Sub-Account**. It uses that phrase with another derivation path; it does not generate a second recovery phrase. Edit the name if needed. The npub and hex public keys appear below their labels in accent color, shortened in the middle. Copy icons copy the complete values. **Advanced** sits below the keys and opens the path editor; leave the proposed path unless you need a specific one.

Follow suggestions show names and small pictures from verified public profiles when available. The extension reuses a shared cache for 30 minutes, keeping at most 500 profiles, and looks up missing metadata at purplepag.es. The public author key is sent to that directory; images load separately from the profile's image host. Missing profiles fall back to a shortened key. Loading does not block selection or **Skip for now**.

The completion screen puts the account summary and **Get Started** at the bottom. It shows the account name and a copyable public key; only derived sub-accounts are described as sharing the main seed phrase. New accounts can use global rules or copy site overrides from another account. Authentication grants stay separate.

posts.title: Understanding the Web of Trust
posts.description: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension builds your trust graph, what hops and trust levels mean, and how trust scores help you decide who to trust on Nostr.
posts.excerpt: The trust graph is the core of the extension. Learn what hops are, how trust scores work, and what the visualization tells you.
posts.seoTitle: Understanding Web of Trust — Nostr WoT Extension
posts.seoDescription: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension builds your trust graph, what hops and trust levels mean, and how trust scores help you decide who to trust on Nostr.
posts.content:
The Web of Trust is the core concept behind the extension. Instead of relying on a central authority to tell you who is trustworthy, you build a trust network from the people you already follow. This guide explains how that network works and what the extension shows you.

## What the Trust Graph Shows

When you open the extension, your trust graph is a visual map of your social connections on Nostr. At the center is you. Radiating outward are the people you follow, the people they follow, and so on. Each node is a Nostr identity, and each connection is a follow relationship.

The graph answers a simple question: how connected is this person to you? Someone deeply embedded in your social network is probably more trustworthy than a brand-new account with no connections to anyone you know.

## Hops Explained

![WoT graph showing multiple hop layers — gateway nodes (gold ring) opened each new layer](/images/guides/understanding-wot/wot-hops-visual.jpg)

Hops measure the shortest path between you and another Nostr user through follow relationships.

### 1st Degree (1 Hop)

These are the people you follow directly. They are your immediate trust circle. The extension assigns the highest trust to these connections because you explicitly chose to follow them.

### 2nd Degree (2 Hops)

These are people followed by the people you follow. You may not know them personally, but someone you trust has chosen to follow them. This is a strong signal — your friends vouch for them by following them.

### 3rd Degree (3 Hops)

Three steps away from you. The connection is weaker but still present. These users are followed by someone who is followed by someone you follow. At this distance, trust is lower but still meaningful — especially if multiple paths connect you.

<Callout type="tip">
The more independent paths that connect you to someone, the higher their trust score. A person reached through five different 2nd-degree connections is more trusted than someone reached through a single 2nd-degree connection.
</Callout>

## How Trust Scores Work

Every Nostr user visible in your trust graph receives a trust score. This score is not an absolute measure of a person's character — it is a measure of how connected they are to your specific network.

The score depends on several factors:

- **Hop distance** — closer connections score higher.
- **Path count** — more paths between you and the user mean a higher score.
- **Network position** — users followed by many of your direct contacts score higher than those connected through a single chain.

The extension normalizes these factors into a score that helps you make quick decisions. When you encounter an unknown profile on a Nostr client, the extension can tell you whether that person is in your trust graph and how strong the connection is.

### Score Ranges

While the exact thresholds are configurable, a typical setup works like this:

- **High trust** — 1st-degree contacts and well-connected 2nd-degree users.
- **Medium trust** — 2nd-degree contacts with fewer paths and some 3rd-degree users with multiple connections.
- **Low trust** — 3rd-degree contacts with thin connections.
- **Unknown** — users with no path to you in the trust graph.

## Trust Is Personal

Your Web of Trust is unique to you. Two people will have completely different trust graphs because they follow different people. There is no global trust score — your graph reflects your social reality on Nostr, not some centralized reputation system. Decentralized trust means no single entity decides who is trustworthy. You and your network do.

## What's Next?

Ready to fine-tune how the extension calculates trust? Head to [Customizing Your Trust Settings](/guides/customizing-trust). Or explore the trust graph visually in the [WoT Playground](/guides/wot-playground).

posts.title: Customizing Your Trust Settings
posts.description: Customize Web of Trust scores with hop weights and path bonuses. Choose local, remote or hybrid queries and review the limits of experimental graph results.
posts.excerpt: Customize Web of Trust scores with hop weights and path bonuses. Choose local, remote or hybrid queries and review the limits of experimental graph results.
posts.seoTitle: Customizing Trust Settings — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Customize Web of Trust scores with hop weights and path bonuses. Choose local, remote or hybrid queries and review the limits of experimental graph results.
posts.content:
Web of Trust scores describe relationships in the follow graph, not a guarantee that a person is safe or trustworthy. The extension’s Web of Trust feature is experimental; results may be incomplete or outdated.

## Open the settings

Open **Settings → Web of Trust (experimental)**. Enable it if you want connected sites with identity access to use `window.nostr.wot`.

**Sync settings** controls the query mode and graph limits. Local mode uses your local graph. Remote and hybrid queries may contact the configured oracle. Choose a maximum depth from one to three hops and review the storage limits before syncing.

![Web of Trust settings and public-key lookup](/images/guides/extension/web-of-trust.png)

## Customize score calculation

Beside **Score calculation**, select the settings icon labelled **Customize scoring**. The current panel has numeric fields, not a sensitivity slider:

- **Hop weights** set the contribution for distances of one, two and three hops. Defaults are 1, 0.5 and 0.25.
- **Path bonuses** for two and three hops default to 0.15 and 0.1.
- **Maximum path bonus** defaults to 0.5.

Use values from 0 to 1. Valid changes are saved automatically. **Reset scoring** restores the default values. Known muted targets score zero regardless of these weights; private mutes must be decrypted first.

![Current score settings with hop weights, path bonuses and a reset button](/images/guides/extension/trust-scoring.png)

## Check the result

Return to **Score calculation**, enter an npub or hex public key and select **Calculate score**. The lookup uses the saved query mode, scoring settings and mute rules. Review its context before using the number to make a decision.

See [Understanding Web of Trust](/guides/understanding-wot) and the [WoT Playground](/guides/wot-playground).

posts.title: Setting Up Your Wallet
posts.description: Connect a Lightning wallet to the Nostr WoT Extension. Compare Quick Setup, NWC and LNbits API access, with setup guides for Alby Hub and LNbits.
posts.excerpt: The extension supports Quick Setup, Nostr Wallet Connect and LNbits API access. Choose the connection that fits your wallet.
posts.seoTitle: Setting Up Your Wallet — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Connect a Lightning wallet to the Nostr WoT Extension. Compare Quick Setup, NWC and LNbits API access, with setup guides for Alby Hub and LNbits.
posts.content:
The Nostr WoT Extension connects to a Lightning wallet so you can check your balance, receive sats and approve payments in your browser. Open the extension, go to **Wallet**, and choose **Quick Setup**, **NWC** or **LNbits**.

If you already use Alby Hub, its app connections are a convenient starting point. For an existing LNbits wallet, direct API access needs fewer setup steps; NWC offers separate connection permissions and budgets. The connection method does not determine who holds your funds: that depends on the wallet and its operator.

For detailed steps, follow our [Alby Hub guide](/guides/alby-hub-nwc) or [LNbits guide](/guides/lnbits-wallet-setup).

## Quick Setup

Choose **Quick Setup** to create a custodial wallet with the configured provider. Once creation succeeds, use **Deposit** to generate a Lightning invoice. The provider holds the funds; NWC and LNbits are not automatically self-custodial alternatives.

<a id="alby-hub" className="block scroll-mt-32" />

## Alby Hub through NWC

Start with an operational Alby Hub and its Lightning wallet.

1. In Alby Hub, open **Connections → Add Connection**.
2. Create a dedicated connection named **Nostr WoT**. Choose permissions, a spending budget and, optionally, an expiry date.
3. Allow wallet information (`get_info`) for connection validation. Add balance, outgoing payments, invoice creation, invoice lookup and transaction history only as needed. These control which extension features are available.
4. Copy the complete pairing secret, beginning with `nostr+walletconnect://`.
5. In the extension, select **NWC**, paste the secret and choose **Connect**.

Keep this secret private: its permissions can authorize spending. Manage or revoke the connection in Alby Hub. See the [official Alby Hub connection guide](https://guides.getalby.com/user-guide/alby-hub/app-connections).

<a id="lnbits-nwc" className="block scroll-mt-32" />

## LNbits through NWC

1. Ask the instance administrator to install and configure **NWC Service Provider**, including a relay at `/nwcprovider/admin`.
2. Open that extension in LNbits, select your wallet and add a connection with **+**.
3. Enable wallet information and the operations you need. Set a budget and expiry where available.
4. Create the connection and copy its pairing URL.
5. Paste it into the Nostr WoT Extension's **NWC** tab and connect.

An LNbits login alone does not create an NWC connection. The [official provider guide](https://docs.lnbits.com/extensions/nwcprovider/) covers the administrator's relay setup and the wallet's connection form.

<a id="lnbits-api" className="block scroll-mt-32" />

## LNbits through its API

1. Open the specific wallet in LNbits and find **API info** or its API documentation panel.
2. Copy the wallet's **Admin API key**.
3. In the extension's **LNbits** tab, enter the instance's HTTPS URL and that key, then connect.

The Admin API key is a wallet credential, **not your administrator login password**. It permits outgoing payments. The invoice/read key cannot send funds and is not interchangeable with the spending key required for the complete wallet flow. See [where LNbits displays its API keys](https://docs.lnbits.com/api/authentication#finding-your-keys). An NWC pairing URL belongs in the **NWC** tab, not the API-key field.

## Other wallets and connection checks

For YakiHonne, copy or export an NWC secret when your wallet offers that option. Other NWC providers follow the same paste-and-connect flow; supported operations depend on their implementation and permissions.

BTCPay Server's standard Nostr plugin connects **to** an external NWC wallet. It does not issue a connection secret for this extension. Use a separate connection from the actual wallet or its NWC bridge; see [BTCPay's Lightning options](https://docs.btcpayserver.org/LightningNetwork/).

After connecting, check your balance and history. If a feature is unavailable, review permissions, expiry and wallet connectivity. If a payment's outcome is unknown, check wallet history before paying again. To change wallets, disconnect in wallet settings and return to setup.

Next, learn about [zaps and automatic approval](/guides/zapping-auto-approve) or [Lightning Addresses](/guides/lightning-address).

posts.title: Zapping and Auto-Approve
posts.description: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension acts as a WebLN provider for zapping, and how to configure auto-approve thresholds for frictionless micropayments.
posts.excerpt: Zap notes without switching apps. Learn how WebLN works in the extension and how auto-approve makes small zaps instant.
posts.seoTitle: Zapping and Auto-Approve — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Learn how the Nostr WoT Extension acts as a WebLN provider for zapping, and how to configure auto-approve thresholds for frictionless micropayments.
posts.content:
Zapping is one of the best parts of Nostr — you see a great note, you send some sats, the person gets rewarded. The extension makes this seamless by acting as a WebLN provider, and auto-approve takes it a step further by removing the confirmation step for small amounts.

## What Is WebLN?

WebLN is a standard that lets websites request Lightning payments through a browser extension. When a Nostr client wants to send a zap, it calls `window.webln.sendPayment()` and the extension handles the rest.

You do not need to configure anything for WebLN to work. Once your wallet is connected, the extension automatically registers itself as the WebLN provider for any site you visit.

## How Zapping Works

Here is the flow when you zap a note on a Nostr client:

1. You click the zap button on a note and choose an amount.
2. The Nostr client creates a Lightning invoice and sends it to the extension via WebLN.
3. The extension shows you a confirmation popup with the amount, recipient, and the note being zapped.
4. You click **Approve**, the extension pays the invoice from your connected wallet.
5. The zap event is published to Nostr, and the recipient sees it.

The entire process happens within your browser. No switching to a separate wallet app, no copying invoices.

<Callout type="tip">
If you see "No WebLN provider found" on a Nostr client, make sure the extension is unlocked and a wallet is connected. Some clients may need a page refresh to detect the provider.
</Callout>

## Setting Up Auto-Approve

For frequent zappers, confirming every 21-sat zap gets tedious. Auto-approve lets you set a threshold — any zap at or below that amount goes through instantly without a popup.

### Configuring the Threshold

1. Click the extension icon and go to the **Wallet** tab.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Find the **Auto-Approve Threshold** field.
4. Enter your preferred amount in sats. For example, `100` means any zap of 100 sats or less is approved automatically.
5. Save. The setting takes effect immediately.

### How It Works

When a site requests a payment via WebLN:

- If the amount is at or below your threshold, the extension pays it silently. No popup, no interruption.
- If the amount is above your threshold, you see the normal confirmation popup.
- If auto-approve is set to `0`, every payment requires manual approval.

This means you can scroll through your feed, zap notes freely with small amounts, and never break your flow. Larger payments still require your explicit approval for safety.

### Per-Site Behavior

Auto-approve respects the extension's [site permissions](/guides/site-permissions). If a site does not have WebLN permission, auto-approve does not apply — the site cannot request payments at all.

## Monitoring Your Zaps

Every zap, whether auto-approved or manually confirmed, appears in your transaction history on the Wallet tab. You can review what was sent, to whom, and when.

If you notice unexpected auto-approved payments, lower your threshold or revoke the site's WebLN permission.

## Recommended Thresholds

- **21 sats** — the classic Nostr micro-zap. Conservative and safe.
- **100 sats** — covers most casual zapping.
- **500 sats** — for power users who zap frequently.
- **0 sats** — disables auto-approve entirely.

<Callout type="tip">
Start with a lower threshold and increase it once you are comfortable with the flow. You can always change it from the wallet settings.
</Callout>

## What's Next?

If you set up your wallet with Quick Setup, you can [claim your own Lightning Address](/guides/lightning-address). To control which sites can request payments, read about [site permissions](/guides/site-permissions).

posts.title: Claiming Your Lightning Address
posts.description: Claim a Lightning Address like yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com through the Nostr WoT Extension and start receiving zaps to a memorable, human-readable address.
posts.excerpt: Get a Lightning Address like yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com. Claim it in seconds and add it to your Nostr profile.
posts.seoTitle: Claim Your Lightning Address — Nostr WoT Extension
posts.seoDescription: Claim a Lightning Address like yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com through the Nostr WoT Extension and start receiving zaps to a memorable, human-readable address.
posts.content:
A Lightning Address is a human-readable identifier — like an email address — that anyone can use to send you sats. Instead of generating invoices manually, you give people your address and they zap you directly. The extension lets you claim one for free when you use Quick Setup.

## What Is a Lightning Address?

A Lightning Address looks like `yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com`. Under the hood, it resolves to a Lightning invoice endpoint. When someone sends sats to your address, the system generates a fresh invoice and routes the payment to your wallet. The sender does not need to know anything about your wallet setup.

Think of it as a permanent, memorable way for people to pay you with Bitcoin over Lightning.

## Claiming Your Address

You need to have a wallet connected via Quick Setup to claim a Lightning Address. If you used NWC or LNbits, your address is managed by your own infrastructure.

1. Open the extension and go to the **Wallet** tab.
2. Click **Settings** or look for the **Lightning Address** section.
3. Enter the username you want. It will become `yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com`.
4. Click **Claim**.
5. If the name is available, it is yours immediately.

<Callout type="tip">
Usernames must be 3-30 characters long and can include lowercase letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens. They are first come, first served, so claim yours early.
</Callout>

## Adding to Your Nostr Profile

After claiming your address, you want it visible on your Nostr profile so people know where to zap you.

### Automatic Method

The extension offers to add your Lightning Address to your Nostr profile automatically right after you claim it. Click **Yes, update my profile** and the extension signs and publishes an updated kind 0 event with your new address.

### Manual Method

If you prefer to do it yourself:

1. Go to the **Identity** tab in the extension.
2. Click **Edit Profile**.
3. Find the **Lightning Address** field (sometimes labeled `lud16`).
4. Enter your full address: `yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com`.
5. Click **Save**.

Either way, Nostr clients will display a zap button on your profile that uses this address.

## Receiving Zaps

Once your Lightning Address is set and published to your profile:

- Anyone viewing your profile on Primal, Snort, Coracle, or other Nostr clients will see a zap option.
- They click zap, choose an amount, and the payment routes to your wallet.
- You see the incoming sats in your wallet balance and transaction history.

No invoices to generate, no QR codes to share. The address handles everything.

## Sharing Your Address

Beyond your Nostr profile, you can share your Lightning Address in social media bios, on your website, or in email signatures. Anyone with a Lightning wallet can send sats to `yourname@zaps.nostr-wot.com` — they do not need to be on Nostr.

## Changing Your Address

If you want a different username, open the Lightning Address settings in the extension and claim a new one. Your old address will stop working, so update your Nostr profile and any other places where you shared it.

<Callout type="tip">
Before changing your address, make sure no recurring services or integrations depend on the old one. The switch is instant and the old address is released.
</Callout>

## What's Next?

Now that people can zap you, learn how to [control which sites can access your wallet](/guides/site-permissions). Or explore the [zapping and auto-approve features](/guides/zapping-auto-approve) to streamline your outgoing zaps.

posts.title: Site Permissions
posts.description: Control which websites can access your Nostr identity, request signatures, and make Lightning payments using the Nostr WoT Extension's permission system.
posts.excerpt: The extension gives you granular control over what each website can do. Learn how per-site permissions keep your keys and sats safe.
posts.seoTitle: Managing Site Permissions — Nostr WoT Extension
posts.seoDescription: Control which websites can access your Nostr identity, request signatures, and make Lightning payments using the Nostr WoT Extension's permission system.
posts.content:
Connection consent, ordinary signing rules and authentication permissions are separate controls. Open **Permissions** in the extension for the active account.

## Global rules and the current website

**Global rules** applies ordinary defaults across connected sites and accounts. **Site rules** opens the website in the current browser tab, not a saved-site list. Visit a normal web page first if the extension asks you to choose a site. The dashboard's Manage permissions shortcut opens the same editor.

Global rules appears above Site rules in the menu. In a site editor, **Add rule** sits beside the website name. The footer's **Global rules** button opens the shared defaults. Global rules has **Go to current site rules** below its content. Back returns to Permissions when opened from that menu.

Gray rows in Site rules are inherited from the visible Global rules. Colored rows are overrides for this account and website. Changing an inherited rule creates an override; **Use inherited default** removes it. Old shared rules migrate once into Global rules; conflicting site choices remain explicit overrides.

## Add, change or reset a rule

Use **Add rule** to choose an action and set **Allow**, **Deny** or **Ask**. A matching site override replaces its global default. Broader rules can still affect the result: a broader denial must be changed separately. These settings cover actions such as reading a public key, signing event kinds, and encrypting or decrypting messages. They do not authorize a new site connection or replace backend/relay authentication consent.

**Reset site overrides** asks for confirmation, removes this account's rules for the current site and keeps you in the same editor. Only inherited global rows remain gray. Removing an override can make a global Allow apply again. **Reset all account overrides** in Global rules also asks for confirmation and keeps globals; neither reset removes separate authentication grants.

A declined current site opens its dismissal editor instead. Choose one week, one month, one year or forever, or remove the dismissal so it can ask again. This does not connect the site or grant signing permission.

## Review a request

**Approve once** and **Deny** resolve the current request; once is not a browser-session permission. Arrow menus offer remembered choices. Grouped requests let you select the requests to approve and deny the displayed group. New or unselected requests are not silently included.

Signing review describes the action and shows note content or a supported event preview. The code icon opens raw event data in a popup. Private-message requests group by sender when available. Click the blurred content to reveal it locally; it hides again after 30 seconds. Revealing does not approve delivery of the decrypted message to the website.

## Backend, relay and wallet permissions

**Default backend auth** starts off for each account. If enabled, connected sites can authenticate with NIP-98 to the exact same HTTPS origin or a verified registry pair. Explicit denials win. **Backend authentication** shows the enabled policy, a rules/registry link and explicit saved grants. Automatic policy approvals do not add individual rows. See the [backend guide](/guides/backend-authentication).

**Relay authentication** manages each relay for the active account, including selected connected apps or all connected sites. It is separate from the read/write relay configuration. See the [relay guide](/guides/relay-authentication).

Lightning payments retain their own confirmation, limits and [automatic payment settings](/guides/zapping-auto-approve). Allowing ordinary Nostr signatures does not create unrestricted payment authority.

posts.title: The WoT Playground
posts.description: Explore the Nostr WoT Playground to visualize your trust graph, filter connections by hop distance, and see how your Web of Trust connects you to the network.
posts.excerpt: The WoT Playground lets you explore your trust graph visually. Filter by hops, search for users, and understand your network at a glance.
posts.seoTitle: The WoT Playground — Nostr WoT Extension Guide
posts.seoDescription: Explore the Nostr WoT Playground to visualize your trust graph, filter connections by hop distance, and see how your Web of Trust connects you to the network.
posts.content:
The WoT Playground is an interactive visualization of your entire trust network. It takes the abstract concept of a Web of Trust and makes it tangible — you can see exactly how you connect to any user on Nostr, explore clusters of trust, and discover patterns in your social graph.

## Accessing the Playground

![WoT Playground initial state — click the root node to start exploring](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-initial.jpg)

There are two ways to open the Playground:

1. **From the extension** — click the extension icon and select **Playground** from the navigation menu.
2. **From the website** — visit the [WoT Playground](/playground) page directly.

The Playground loads your trust graph data from the extension. If you are not signed in or the extension is locked, you will be prompted to unlock it first.

## The Trust Graph Visualization

The main view is an interactive graph where nodes represent Nostr users and edges represent follow relationships.

### Reading the Graph

![Trust graph with hop-1 follows expanded — color-coded by trust score](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-graph-expanded.jpg)

- **Your node** sits at the center, highlighted distinctly.
- **1st-degree connections** (direct follows) appear closest to you, typically in a bright color.
- **2nd-degree connections** form the next ring, in a slightly muted tone.
- **3rd-degree connections** are at the outer edges, more faded.
- **Edge lines** connect nodes to show follow relationships. Thicker or brighter lines may indicate stronger trust scores.

<Callout type="tip">
Click and drag to pan around the graph. Use your scroll wheel or pinch gesture to zoom in and out. Click on any node to see details about that user.
</Callout>

### Node Details

![Node detail panel showing trust score, hop distance, and trust path](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-node-detail-v2.jpg)

Click on any node to open a detail panel showing:

- Profile information (name, avatar, npub).
- Trust score relative to you.
- Hop distance.
- Number of paths connecting you.

Click **View Profile** to open a full profile preview:

![Profile modal showing avatar, bio, trust path and recent notes](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-profile-modal.jpg)

- Profile information (name, avatar, npub).
- Trust score relative to you.
- Hop distance.
- Number of paths connecting you.
- Mutual follows — people you both follow.

This is useful for understanding why someone has a particular trust score and how they connect to your network.

## Filtering and Searching

The Playground includes tools to narrow your view and find specific information.

### Filtering by Hops

![Filters sidebar with multiple layers expanded and gateway nodes visible](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-filters.jpg)

Use the hop filter to show only connections at a specific distance:

- **1 hop** — shows only your direct follows. Useful for reviewing your inner circle.
- **2 hops** — adds friends-of-friends. This is where most of your day-to-day interactions happen.
- **3 hops** — the full graph. Shows the outer boundary of your trust network.

Toggle these filters using the controls in the sidebar or toolbar.

### List View

![List view showing all nodes sorted by trust score with distance and paths](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-list-view.jpg)

Switch to **List** view to see all nodes in a sortable table. You can sort by trust score, distance, or name — useful for scanning your full trust network at a glance.

### Searching for Users

Type a name, npub, or NIP-05 identifier into the search bar. If the user is in your trust graph, the visualization highlights their node and shows the path between you.

If they are not in your graph, the search tells you so — which itself is useful information. An unknown user means they have no connection to your network within the configured hop distance.

## Analyzing Your Network

Beyond browsing, the Playground helps you understand the structure of your trust network.

### Expanding Layers

![Expanded node (gold ring) with its hop-2 follows orbiting around it](/images/guides/wot-playground/playground-gateway-node.jpg)

When you expand a node, it gets a **gold ring** to mark it as a gateway — the entry point into a new layer of your network. Its follows appear as a new orbit around it. You can expand multiple nodes to explore different branches of your Web of Trust.

### Cluster Detection

The visualization often reveals clusters — groups of densely connected users. These typically correspond to communities. You might see a cluster of Bitcoin developers, another of artists, and another of local friends. The visual grouping helps you understand the different social circles that make up your Web of Trust.

### Bridge Users

Some nodes connect otherwise separate clusters. These bridge users span different communities in your network and often have high trust scores due to multiple independent paths. If your graph is small or sparse, consider following more people to strengthen your Web of Trust.

<Callout type="tip">
The Playground is a read-only visualization. Nothing you do here changes your trust settings or follow list. Explore freely.
</Callout>

## What's Next?

Now that you have explored your trust graph, you might want to [customize your trust settings](/guides/customizing-trust) based on what you discovered. Or head back to the [getting started guide](/guides/getting-started) to review the fundamentals.

posts.title: Connect Alby Hub with NWC
posts.description: Connect Alby Hub to Nostr WoT with a dedicated NWC connection. Choose permissions, check your balance, and manage access in your Hub.
posts.excerpt: Connect Alby Hub to Nostr WoT with a dedicated NWC connection. Choose permissions, check your balance, and manage access in your Hub.
posts.seoTitle: Connect Alby Hub with NWC
posts.seoDescription: Connect Alby Hub to Nostr WoT with a dedicated NWC connection. Choose permissions, check your balance, and manage access in your Hub.
posts.content: Alby Hub can connect your existing Lightning wallet to the Nostr WoT Extension through Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC). Start with an Alby Hub that is already running, reachable, and funded. This guide covers connecting that wallet, not installing Hub or opening Lightning channels. ## Create a connection in Alby Hub Open your Hub and go to **Connections → Add Connection**. Give this connection a recognizable name, such as “Nostr WoT browser”. A separate connection makes it easier to identify its activity and withdraw access later. Alby's [app connections guide](https://guides.getalby.com/user-guide/alby-hub/app-connections) explains its permission, budget, and expiration controls. Choose permissions for the features you want: - **Wallet information (`get_info`)** is required for the extension's connection check. - **Balance (`get_balance`)** lets the extension display your sats. - **Payments (`pay_invoice`)** allows sending payments. - **Invoices (`make_invoice`, `lookup_invoice`)** supports creating and checking deposit invoices. - **History (`list_transactions`)** lets the extension show recent transactions. Set a spending budget you are comfortable granting to this browser connection. Review whether it renews, and choose an expiration date if appropriate. A budget set in Hub and an automatic approval threshold in the extension are separate controls. Check both before enabling unattended payments. ## Paste the NWC connection secret Complete the connection in Hub and copy the full URI beginning with `nostr+walletconnect://`. The URI is a credential. Anyone holding it may exercise its granted permissions. Keep it out of screenshots, support messages, shared documents, and public posts. Open the Nostr WoT Extension, go to **Wallet**, select **NWC**, paste the URI, and connect. The first-use help popup explains the available wallet options. Its opt-out lets you stop showing that help automatically; it does not change wallet permissions. Alby's [NWC link tutorial](https://guides.getalby.com/user-guide/browser-extension/link-wallet/alby-hub-via-nwc-link) demonstrates pairing with **Alby's own extension**. For Nostr WoT, use the Wallet → NWC steps above. ## Verify access without sending a payment If you granted balance access, compare the displayed balance with Hub. Check history if you enabled that permission. Connecting does not require a test payment. If a feature fails, review its permission and the connection's expiration in Hub before replacing the secret. NWC describes the connection between applications. Custody and fund recovery depend on your wallet and hosting arrangement; choosing a protocol alone does not determine them. If a payment reports an **unknown outcome**, check Hub's payment history before starting another attempt. A missing reply does not establish that payment failed. To withdraw access, revoke this app connection in Hub; disconnecting the extension alone is not a substitute. Return to the [wallet overview](/guides/setting-up-wallet), or follow the [LNbits setup guide](/guides/lnbits-wallet-setup) for that provider.

posts.title: Connect LNbits to Nostr WoT
posts.description: Connect your LNbits wallet to Nostr WoT through NWC or its API. Find the right credentials, set permissions and check balance, invoices and payment history.
posts.excerpt: Choose an NWC connection with its own limits or connect directly with your LNbits wallet API key.
posts.content:
LNbits can connect to the Nostr WoT Extension in two ways: **Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC)** or the wallet's **HTTP API**. This guide starts with an existing LNbits wallet. Your instance operator and funding source determine who holds your funds; choosing NWC or API access does not change that.

## Choose your connection

Use **NWC** for a dedicated app connection with its own permissions, spending limits and expiry. Your LNbits administrator must first enable the NWC provider extension. Use the **LNbits** tab for direct API access when you already have your wallet's spending key and instance URL. It needs fewer setup steps, but shares the wallet's API credential rather than a separate NWC allowance.

<a id="lnbits-nwc" className="block scroll-mt-32" />

## Connect through NWC

### Prepare the LNbits instance

The instance administrator installs **NWC Service Provider** and configures its relay at `/nwcprovider/admin`. A relay carries the connection's messages. If you use someone else's instance and cannot see this extension, ask its operator whether it is available. A normal LNbits login does not create an NWC connection.<Citation id="1" />

### Create your app connection

1. Open **NWC Service Provider** in LNbits and select the wallet you want to use.
2. Choose **+** to add a connection. Give it a recognizable name, such as **Nostr WoT**.
3. Enable wallet information (`get_info`), which the extension needs to validate the connection. Enable balance, outgoing payments, invoice creation, invoice lookup and transaction history according to the features you want.
4. Set a spending limit and expiry where available. These limits belong to this connection.
5. Create the connection, choose **Connect**, and copy its complete pairing URL, beginning with `nostr+walletconnect://`.
6. Open **Wallet → NWC** in the Nostr WoT Extension, paste the URL and choose **Connect**.

Keep the pairing URL private. Anyone holding it can use the permissions you granted. Manage or revoke this connection in LNbits when you no longer need it.

<a id="lnbits-api" className="block scroll-mt-32" />

## Connect through the LNbits API

1. Open the specific wallet in LNbits. Find **API info** or the wallet's API documentation panel.
2. Copy its **Admin API key**. LNbits also displays an invoice/read key; that key cannot send payments.<Citation id="2" />
3. In the Nostr WoT Extension, open **Wallet → LNbits**.
